subject: Re: Cross-border tenant custody & failover coordination

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-pay.com>

Cc: Gonzalo Ruiz <gonzalo@acme-pay.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:23:00 +0000
Subject: Cross-border tenant custody & failover coordination

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we lock the Mutual Action Plan I need a few confirmations about how data custody and networking behave if we trigger failover from our EU private deployment into APAC warm-standby (scoped to the tenant). Specifically: 

- Will customer data (request/response payloads and KV cache) ever be persisted to APAC storage outside of the EU copy unless we explicitly sign off on a custody transfer?
- If a disaster causes failover, what happens to KMS keys? Do you support a customer-managed KMS that stays in the EU, or will Redwood generate ephemeral keys in APAC?
- What are the exact egress implications if our traffic routes through APAC (IP blocks, expected AS paths, and any third-party peering)? We need this for our legal and network teams.
- Can you outline the activation window and the expected RTO/RPO under the Dedicated private deployment SLA?

We also need a list of artifacts for our auditors (custody mapping diagram, control-plane handshake evidence, and a DR test runbook). Can you drop those into the shared folder and propose a 2-week test window?

Best,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure Security | Acme Payments
alice@acme-pay.com
+44 20 5555 2345

Attachments: (none)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Gonzalo Ruiz <gonzalo@acme-pay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-border tenant custody & failover coordination

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, details and artifacts below. I attached the custody mapping diagram as requested.

Summary (short):
- We do not persist primary customer data in APAC unless you authorize a custody failover. Warm-standby keeps a replayable EU snapshot; writes are quarantined until custody is accepted.
- KMS: by default we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) with keys anchored in EU. During a declared emergency we can support wrapped ephemeral keys in APAC under a documented key-wrap handshake, but the wrapped keys reference EU root key material (customer controls unwrap).
- Networking/egress: failover will announce traffic from our APAC edge ASN ranges; we will provide the specific IP blocks and peering partners in the attached diagram and the Drive link. There is no third-party cloud peering beyond standard IX partners unless you opt into a marketplace integration.
- SLA expectations: for Dedicated private deployments our documented RTO is 15 minutes (control-plane failover) and RPO is 1 hour for tenant-scoped warm-standby by default. We can tighten RPO with a higher replication cadence (cost tradeoff).

What I dropped into the shared Drive: custody-mapping-diagram.pdf (attached), a short checklist, and a placeholder Mutual Action Plan draft (mutual-action-plan.docx). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3CustodyPlaybook

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether Acme will keep KMS root keys in your EU KMS (preferred). If yes, tell us the KMS contact and the key policy point person.
2) Schedule a 90-minute DR test window in the next 2 weeks where we perform a failover dry-run (no custody accept) and a second window a week later for a custody-switch acceptance test (full write acceptance).
3) We’ll circulate the kms-ops-checklist.xlsx for your ops to complete 48 hours before the first dry-run.

I'll loop Marissa to confirm contractual notes (RTO/RPO and any rollback windows).

—
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: custody-mapping-diagram.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-border tenant custody & failover coordination

Hi Alice — looping in operational details and acceptance criteria.

Operational bullets:
- RTO/RPO: Confirming Logan's numbers: RTO target 15 minutes (control-plane switchover + route convergence), RPO default 1 hour (async replication). If Acme needs RPO <= 15 minutes we can run near-sync at additional cost; we will include cost delta in the MAP.
- Failover mode: warm-standby (read-only in APAC snapshot) by default. We only switch writes to APAC on an explicit custody-authorized action signed by an Acme admin.
- KMS handshake: we require a KMS contact and a short HSM policy excerpt to specify key-wrapping behavior. See kms-ops-checklist.xlsx (attached).
- Network controls: we will provide exact BGP prep (ASNs and prefix lists) and a temporary ACL recipe so your infra can allowlist our APAC edges for the test.

Pre-test checklist highlights (to complete 48h prior):
- Confirm KMS contact + test unwrapping authority (person + email)
- Provide an allowlist window for APAC edge IPs (we'll supply limits)
- Review the mutual-action-plan.docx and mark any legal exceptions (rollback SLA, data export acceptance criteria)

I attached the kms-ops-checklist.xlsx. Once we have the KMS contact we’ll coordinate a brief call with your security engineer to validate the unwrap flow. Proposed dry-run window: Tue 25 May 2027 09:00–10:30 UTC. Custody-switch target: Tue 01 Jun 2027 09:00–10:30 UTC (contingent on dry-run).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
